issues.title: Priority 2 external-report dedup check only scans open-issues.json, not closed-issues.json
issues.description: decider.md Priority 2 dispatcher check (`ls monitor/external-reports/report-*.json ... o.issues.some(i=>i.source&&i.source.includes(...))`) reads only monitor/decisions/open-issues.json. FUSE cannot unlink files, so tombstoned/superseded external-report files (report-1.json, report-1-devilwench-friendly-meta.json) persist forever and re-trigger NEW on every decider run even after being closed as wontfix. This has produced at least 9 duplicate wontfix closures for the same GitHub issue #1 report (ISS-1982, ISS-1983, ISS-2071, ISS-2072, ISS-1448, ISS-674, ISS-698, ISS-2923, ISS-2958). Fix candidate: extend the dedup check in decider.md to also scan closed-issues.json for a matching source, or add a tombstone_status convention to external-report files (mirroring the stranded-patches tombstone convention already documented in decider-patches-and-selfapply.md) that the Priority 2 check honors.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend Priority 2 dedup bash/node check to scan closed-issues.json in addition to open-issues.json, OR adopt tombstone_status:"closed-no-action" convention on report JSON files that the check honors before flagging NEW.
issues.escalation_reason: BAU triage: narrowness gate fails NOT_NEVER_PUSH — target is monitor/prompts/decider.md (Priority 2 dispatcher bash block), which is in the NEVER_PUSH list per routing-matrix.md rule 3. Well-specified fix (scan closed-issues.json in addition to open-issues.json in the dedup check, or add a tombstone_status convention to external-report files) but requires operator-applied prompt-file edit.

issues.description: priority-queue.json carries three stray, non-schema top-level fields introduced 2026-07-18 by an operator cowork edit (file last_updated=2026-07-18T08:45Z, by=steve operator via cowork) and never removed since (decider pop/push only rewrites the queue array): queue_length:1, queue_depth:1, next_queue_id:587. Per DATA-SCHEMAS.md the live queue file carries ONLY the active queue + schema metadata + next_id; these three are not in the schema. queue_length and queue_depth are read by NOTHING (queue depth is computed live from pq.queue.length) -- pure cosmetic cruft. next_queue_id is NOT harmless: lint-decider-surfaces.js lines 209 and 219 read it as a FALLBACK for next_id (next_id if non-null else next_queue_id if non-null else null). It is stale-low (587 vs canonical next_id 591). Today masked because next_id is present; but if any future edit drops or nulls next_id, the lint silently falls back to 587 and would authorize reuse of queue_ids 587-590 -- the exact queue_id-collision class PROP-089/lint exists to prevent. A poisoned fallback in the trust path. Went uncaught for 6 days because nothing lints the queue file's own top-level field-set for schema conformance (the lint validates issue surfaces + next-id monotonicity but does not reject unknown/stale shadow fields on priority-queue.json).
issues.source: curmudgeon-verify no-op-run observation (flagged in summary, no write access to queue) + operator-cowork verification 2026-07-24
issues.notes: OPERATOR OWNS THE LIVE-DATA CLEANUP. The one-time removal of the three stray fields from priority-queue.json (esp. clearing the stale next_queue_id:587) will be applied by the operator directly -- priority-queue.json is operator/decider-owned and this is operator-introduced cruft, so tinker should NOT edit the queue data. Assume the operator clears the value. Tinker scope is the STRUCTURAL fix only.
issues.routing_reason: Structural/lint hardening is tinker-lane: (1) harden lint-decider-surfaces.js so next_id is required (drop the next_queue_id fallback, fail-closed) OR gate the fallback with a monotonic sanity floor (fallback must be >= max allocated queue_id across live+archive); (2) add a schema-conformance guard rejecting unknown top-level fields on priority-queue.json, mirroring the PROP-089/PROP-106 lint discipline, so operator/decider edits cannot silently reintroduce shadow fields. Recurrence-prevention is the real deliverable; the data cleanup is a one-off the operator handles.
issues.operator_progress: [2026-07-26] Operator cleared the live-data half: removed the three stray fields (queue_length, queue_depth, next_queue_id:587) from priority-queue.json. Canonical fields intact (next_id=591, depth=1, empty array); verified no lost item (next_id advanced 587->591 = 4 items pushed+popped since the 2026-07-18 snapshot, all accounted for). REMAINING tinker scope is Phase-2 STRUCTURAL only: (a) harden lint-decider-surfaces.js so next_id is required / floor the next_queue_id fallback, (b) add schema-conformance rejection of unknown top-level fields on priority-queue.json so this cruft cannot silently reappear. Do NOT re-flag the data cleanup as operator-owed; it is done.
